summary_paragraph: A woman with end-stage renal disease, type II diabetes, and a history of recurrent dialysis line infections was admitted due to purulent drainage from her left tunneled hemodialysis catheter. She presented with hyperkalemia (potassium 7.2) and was treated with intravenous calcium, insulin, dextrose, and kayexalate. The infected catheter was removed, and a temporary femoral line was placed when attempts to access the internal jugular veins failed due to bilateral thromboses. She received intravenous vancomycin and ceftazidime for a catheter-related infection caused by Proteus mirabilis and MSSA. During her stay, she developed symptoms of uremia, including chest pain and sleepiness, which resolved after resuming dialysis. A permanent left external jugular dialysis catheter was successfully placed, and the femoral line was removed. She began accepting CPAP for her obstructive sleep apnea during the admission. Her blood pressure was supported with midodrine during dialysis, and warfarin was continued for her history of deep venous thrombosis. She was discharged in stable condition to extended care to complete her antibiotic course.
